newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Mafia suspect linked to ex-Collor aide arrested.
newsitem.headline: Mafia suspect linked to ex-Collor aide arrested.

text.p: Brazilian police said on Friday they had arrested an Italian man believed to be a member of the Mafia and suspected of having had money laundering ties with a murdered aide of disgraced former President Fernando Collor.

A police spokeswoman said 56-year-old Domenico Verde was arrested in Maceio, Alagoas state, on Thursday in response to an extradition request by Italian authorities, who accuse Verde of involvement with the Mafia.
"We are also investigating the possibility that he was involved in money laundering operations with Paulo Cesar Farias, but we cannot say for certain yet," she said.

Brazilian police were given evidence by their Italian colleagues in March of bank transfers worth $7.8 million between former Collor campaign manager Farias and Italian drug traffickers. The transactions were uncovered by Italian police tracing the origin of deposits in Mafia accounts.
The finds came four years after police began investigating an alleged influence-peddling scheme believed to have been masterminded by Farias that forced Collor to resign in 1992.
Verde, who has been living in Brazil since 1993 and has become a naturalised Brazilian, denies being in the Mafia and says he does not know Farias, the police spokeswoman said.

He was listed as living in Rio de Janeiro but has actually been living in Maceio and is building a house near the beach villa where Farias and his girlfriend Suzana Marcolino were found shot to death in June 1996.

Brazilian authorities only recently decided to reopen the probe into the murder after a new forensic report contradicted the earlier official version that it was a crime of passion. The report found no evidence to support the official finding that Farias was shot by Marcolino, who then committed suicide.
